tagline: Across the Continental Divide, from railroad ties to fur-trade meeting grounds.
intro: The Centennial Scenic Byway forms a 163-mile horseshoe between Dubois and Pinedale, crossing badlands, ranch land and high mountain country. Its paved, two-lane roads pass through two national forests and Grand Teton National Park. The Forest Service identifies cultural history and the variety of landscapes and ecosystems as the reasons for its designation. Driving straight through takes about four hours. Along Blackrock Creek, the road passes between broad valleys and meadows and narrower wooded canyons, giving the crossing a changing scale.

The Forest Service byway designation came in 1989, and its name marks Wyoming’s hundredth anniversary of statehood. The corridor’s older journeys included the Jones Expedition, which Togwotee guided across the pass in 1873. Above the Wind River, tie hacks later cut pine into railroad ties and floated them downstream; hand production gave way to mechanization in the 1940s.

Start in Dubois on US 26/287 and climb over the Continental Divide at Togwotee Pass toward Moran Junction. Turn south through Grand Teton National Park toward Jackson, with the Teton Range rising west of the road. Beyond Jackson, continue through Hoback Junction and Bondurant to Pinedale. In Hoback Canyon, the river parallels the highway and crosses beneath it several times.

moments.title: Tie Hack Memorial
moments.text: The Tie Hack Memorial commemorates the men who made railway ties for the Chicago and Northwestern Railway. They cut lodgepole pine in the mountains above the Wind River and sawed it by hand into eight-foot ties. Then they floated the ties downstream to be gathered lower in the valley. Hand production continued until the 1940s, when tie making became mechanized. Dubois retains another trace of that work: remnants of the wooden flumes that carried ties toward the Wind River are visible in the surrounding landscape. Scandinavian immigrants sent ties along those flumes into the river, which carried the wood to Riverton for processing.

moments.title: Togwotee Pass
moments.text: Togwotee Pass carries US 26 and US 287 across the Continental Divide between Dubois and Moran Junction. Its name honors Togwotee, who guided the Jones Expedition over this crossing in 1873. The pass lies between Two Ocean Mountain and Breccia Peak; the Teton Range is visible from its western slopes. From the pass, the Absarokas show cliffs banded with volcanic ash and lava. Winter snowfall often exceeds 25 feet, and blizzards can close the road for days. The crossing provides the most direct approach to Grand Teton National Park from eastern Wyoming.

moments.title: Upper Green River Rendezvous Site
moments.text: No traces of the rendezvous themselves survive at this meeting ground on the Green River. At least five gatherings took place on and near the site, roughly around the river’s confluence with Horse Creek. The rendezvous brought fur trappers together with suppliers and buyers. William Henry Ashley first organized the meetings, giving structure to a dispersed trade. The gatherings spread widely because so many animals needed water and forage. A commemorative marker overlooks the Horse Creek site. Other commemorative markers stand near US 191 at another rendezvous site; the larger meeting ground received National Historic Landmark status in 1961.

practical: Togwotee Pass: The byway operates year-round, with temporary winter closures possible because of snow. (checked 2026-10-11)
